entries.title: Fixed Paired Longitudinal Helical Drums and Bridge Cab Vehicle
entries.description: One wholly newly authored screw-drum vehicle inspired static exterior. Two complete long closed taper-ended drums flank a narrow raised bridge body. Each drum carries one whole continuous thick helical outer flight of opposite handedness and independent complete front/rear stub axles. One connected twin-rail frame with full end crossmembers and four downward end towers joins those longitudinal axles to the full central body, leaving a real open underside between the drums. A short solid faceted forward cab, thick opaque glazing-style panes, a proud roof and separate low tapered rear hood complete the vehicle silhouette. Small lowest flight facets are deliberately flattened for this fixed display stance; they are not a real screw profile or a physical balance simulation. Unlike the old snowmobile there are no front skis, transverse track rollers, central track loop or straddle saddle; unlike the old pedalboat there is no paddle axis, twin seats or floating pontoon bridge. The entire long drum/end-tower/central cab-body architecture is newly drawn, not old vehicle wheels changed to coils, copied floats or more helix turns. One model zero scenes, four opaque constant untextured PBR roles, metres Z up and whole horizontal bounds centred. No occupants, terrain, drivetrain, fuel, engine internals, rotary motion, buoyancy, traction, steering, ground interaction, amphibious or snow performance, real clearances, manufacturing, road suitability, human fit, load or safety capability. Rigging animation interaction not made or verified.

entries.title: Whole Penguin on Fractured Ice Shelf
entries.description: One static cold-region wildlife display scene, one scene and zero new independent models. One entire qualified upright short-neck penguin stands with both complete original webbed foot soles on the real planar top of one entire qualified fractured ice-edge module. The complete head, bill, both flippers, belly, feet, tail and eyes remain unchanged. The full thick ice shelf retains its original through-thickness V fracture, recessed lower body and projecting upper lip; it is neither recoloured nor reshaped around the animal. A single opaque blue scene-only datum surrounds the whole shelf. Unlike the original opposed frozen riverbanks scene, no second bank, snowbank or central river passage is composed; this establishes one actual animal-on-shelf contact with the notch and front undercut left visible. Both entire source GLBs retain all oriented triangles and full constant opaque per-face PBR at unit scale under whole translations only; hierarchy is explicitly baked and faceted normals recomputed. No new penguin or terrain model, no animals multiplied for count. Artistic fixed ecological vignette only, without exact species, geographic locality, habitat suitability, animal care, buoyancy, water or ice simulation, ice strength, safe standing, load, navigation or safety capability. Rigging animation and interaction not made.

entries.title: Static Low Body and Four Spread Leg Water Strider
entries.description: One newly authored complete enlarged stylised wingless water-strider-like insect. A narrow low head and elongated thorax continue into a smooth gently tapering abdomen with pale longitudinal flank strips. Two short folded front limbs contrast with four much longer low-spreading support legs: the middle pair reaches far sideways and the hind pair sweeps back. Their finite flattened tips form a fixed display stance, with no water plane or false ripple pedestal. Two fine forward antennae and two small lateral eye appearances complete the whole. All body stations and limb paths are new, not a mosquito with wings deleted or dragonfly with resized legs. One whole model zero scenes. Static opaque illustrative exterior only, deliberately enlarged; no exact species or biological scale, surface tension, buoyancy, skating, feeding, gait, rigging, animation or habitat performance claim.
